article_title: Cost-effective analysis of teaching pelvic examination skills using Gynaecology Teaching Associates (GTAs) compared with manikin models (The CEAT Study).
citation: Janjua Aisha, Roberts Tracy, Okeahialam Nicola, Clark T Justin. (2018). Cost-effective analysis of teaching pelvic examination skills using Gynaecology Teaching Associates (GTAs) compared with manikin models (The CEAT Study). BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2017-015823
title: Gynaecology Teaching Associate (GTA) programme: trained expert patients who instruct medical students in pelvic examination
description: GTAs are "expert patients known as Gynaecology Teaching Associates (GTAs), who are recruited and trained to instruct medical students in achieving practical experience" of female pelvic examination. In the trial, GTA teaching was a 2-hour session early in a 5-week O&G placement, with students then examined on GTAs by a blinded assessor. GTAs were paid £30 per hour including travel, and a faculty of eight GTAs was recruited by advertisement and formally interviewed.
requirements: GTAs must be recruited (in the trial by poster advertisement and formal interviews) and trained in knowledge, skills and communication by clinical lecturers over multiple supervised sessions
constraints: GTA teaching is an expensive human resource; costs depend on local pay rates and facilities, and GTA availability is largely after clinic hours because GTAs have their own work commitments
target_learning_goals: competence in gynaecological pelvic examination (speculum and bimanual examination)
examples: In the TARGET trial, 241 students received GTA-led teaching in 2-hour sessions during the first week of their O&G placement, compared with 240 receiving manikin teaching
